name: LYGO local engine limbs
what: Local image, sound and video engines a person can install on their own machine and hand to the portal. The portal is the cockpit; the engine stays on their hardware.

bridge.note: Answers CORS and Chrome's Local Network Access preflight; ComfyUI does not, which is why the bridge exists.

limbs.licence: Qwen licence (weights) · ComfyUI build redistributed by Comfy-Org
limbs.picked_on: 11.4M downloads of the ComfyUI build; strong text rendering; a GGUF path that fits 12 GB cards

weights.role: ComfyUI layout: turbo bf16 model 14.2 GB + int8 text encoder 9.35 GB
Q5_K_M 5.4 GB / Q6_K 6.3 GB for 8–12 GB cards

limbs.picked_on: MIT weights, turbo renders a track in seconds on 8 GB, the most-used music model in ComfyUI
the one good video model that fits a desktop: 720p, Apache-2.0, 3.8 GB at Q5 instead of a 34 GB repo

weights.role: every Wan 2.2 variant in ComfyUI layout, including text encoder and VAE

limbs.disk: ~18 GB (Q5 model + fp8 text encoder + VAE)

honesty: Stub mode proves the wiring, never the model. /health says which backend answered.
No weights are mirrored here: every download link is the official Hugging Face repository.
Nothing is uploaded. The bridge binds 127.0.0.1; the portal can reach it and the internet cannot.
One limb is a complete product. The full LYGO console is optional and separate.
